A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same survey, with matching authors, title and core exposition. All 19 pages of v2 and 36 pages of v3 support comparison of text, equations, figures and tables. Both end with references; neither contains a separate appendix.

before.justification: v2 surveys existing TPP research. Its performance and robustness findings are attributed to cited studies; it reports no original experiments, simulations or empirical data analysis.

after.justification: v3 remains a survey. Its new comparison tables and Section 6 summarize literature, benchmark resources and qualitative findings, without reporting original empirical measurements.

M1.justification: Neither version proposes a TPP algorithm or model. The added diffusion, flow and graph-based methods are attributed to prior work; expanded descriptions of existing methods do not establish changes to a procedure proposed by this survey.

E1.justification: New Section 6 catalogs datasets such as Retweet, StackOverflow, Taxi, Amazon and Taobao. This expands surveyed resources, but neither version actually uses datasets or tasks for its own training or evaluation. TESRBench and DanmakuTPPBench were already discussed in v2.

E2.justification: Neither version evaluates baselines against a proposed method. The new tables compare properties of surveyed models and surveys, rather than adding or removing methods from an empirical comparison.

E3.justification: Section 6 adds descriptions of common evaluation tasks, metrics and standardization needs. These are literature guidance, not protocols applied in new experiments or revisions to an existing experiment's settings.

E4.justification: No ablation, sensitivity study or robustness analysis is added or revised. Existing summaries such as observation-noise robustness in Trouleau et al. remain. New discussion of diffusion and multimodal failure conditions supplies interpretation rather than additional experimental analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports empirical run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. Discussion of Bayesian uncertainty and estimator variance concerns methodological properties rather than experimental uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: v2 reports state-of-the-art performance for PromptTPP across three datasets and Language-TPP across five; v3 omits these specific summaries. Section 6 adds qualitative cross-study trends, including Transformer advantages in next-event prediction. These are changes to reported literature findings, not new experimental measurements.

T1.justification: The main TPP definitions, likelihood reasoning and Equations 1–19 remain. Sections 7.3–7.4 add explicit generic NCE and Fisher-divergence objectives in Equations 22–23, with a qualification about defining scores for TPPs. This adds limited formal detail without new theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the central contribution: reviewing Bayesian, neural and LLM approaches through model design, estimation, applications and challenges. Expanded coverage and the survey-comparison table elaborate this existing contribution rather than redefine its main claims.

C2.justification: Section 5 replaces largely positive method summaries with substantive efficiency, reasoning and scalability tradeoffs, and distinguishes probabilistic TPP tasks from retrieval and QA over timestamped data. Sections 4.4, 6 and 9 substantially expand limitations concerning temporal consistency, benchmark comparability, interpretability and multimodal alignment.

D1.justification: v3 newly documents literature-selection criteria in Section 1, describes EasyTPP's implementation and evaluation resources, and adds Taxi and Taobao access references. Section 5.2 also specifies LoRA and an intensity head for TPP-LLM. These are documentation additions, not evidence of changed experiments.

R1.justification: v3 substantially expands coverage of diffusion and flow models, speculative sampling, latent-graph models, event-sequence clustering and benchmarking infrastructure. Examples include Lüdke et al., Kerrigan et al., Yang and Zha, EasyTPP and HyPro. Table 1 also makes the survey's positioning against earlier reviews explicit.

P1.justification: The LLM and Challenges sections undergo substantial paragraph rewrites and expanded comparative explanation. The training exposition is expanded, survey methodology is documented, and dedicated diffusion and benchmark sections alter the narrative structure. These changes extend well beyond citation-style changes and renumbering.

P2.justification: The two-column IEEE-style document becomes a single-column TMLR layout. Table I is redesigned and expanded as Table 4, six other tables are added, and the applications diagram in Figure 7 is replaced by Table 7. Figures 1–6 largely retain their content with changed sizing and placement.

improvement.justification: Compared with v2, the benchmark guide, comparison tables and more critical LLM discussion improve the survey's practical usefulness and balance. These gains are tempered by inconsistencies in the additions: Section 4.4 describes Kerrigan et al. (2024) as diffusion-based, whereas Section 9 and its EventFlow reference identify flow matching. The net improvement is useful but limited.
